title: 5.2.12 Bouncy Ball
description: Learn how bounciness and friction change how sprites feel.

steps.title: Build a box with four walls
steps.instructions: Four static sprites: top, bottom, left, right: make a containment box.
hints: Re-use the same size; just change positions and rotations.

steps.title: Add a ball
steps.instructions: Create a dynamic sprite with a `diameter` (e.g. 30): that makes it a circle collider instead of a rectangle.
hints: new Sprite(200, 100, 30): one size argument = circle.

steps.title: Tune bounciness
steps.instructions: Set `ball.bounciness = 1`. Values above 0.9 make it bounce nearly forever; 0 means it sticks.

steps.title: Try friction
steps.instructions: Give the ball `ball.friction = 0`. Then try `ball.friction = 5`. Notice how it rolls vs. drags.

requirements.title: Create multiple static walls
requirements.description: At least two 'static' sprites (made with 'static', or given .collider = 'static'). Help: 5.2.11 (Bounciness and Friction)

requirements.title: Make it bouncy
requirements.description: The ball's .bounciness is set near the top of the 0 to 1 range: 0.5 or more. Help: 5.2.11 (Bounciness and Friction)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch (p5-style JavaScript with a physics world) for the lab "5.2.12 Bouncy Ball". The task they were given: Build a closed box with a ball in it: turn gravity on, make four long thin static walls (top, bottom, left, right), make the ball as a dynamic sprite with one size number so it is a circle, store it in ball and colour it, make it bouncy (near the top of the 0 to 1 range), give it a friction value (the steps try 0 and then 5), give it a sideways starting speed, and paint the background in draw(). What the starter file already had: `let ball;`, a 400 by 400 canvas, and step comments in setup() and draw(). The starter meets none of the criteria. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do when the sketch runs. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, if / else chains or ternaries, helper functions, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment or inside a string never runs, so a line the student only wrote in a comment does not count. moSHion facts that matter here: A sprite made with 'static' as its last argument never moves or falls; one made without it is dynamic, so gravity and collisions move it. A sprite's body type can also be set afterwards with .collider = 'static'. new Sprite(x, y, d) with one size number makes a circle that many pixels across. bounciness runs from 0 (sticks) to 1 (gives back all its energy). friction is drag along a surface; 0 slides freely. world.gravity.y starts at 0 until a sketch sets it. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise. Write for a 14-year-old reader: short sentences and plain, everyday words.

rubric.title: Create multiple static walls
rubric.description: At least two sprites are static (made with 'static', or given .collider = 'static'). The step asks for four walls; two or more count for this card. Help: 5.2.11 (Bounciness and Friction)

rubric.title: Create a dynamic ball
rubric.description: At least one sprite is made without the static body type, so it is dynamic and can move: that is the ball. A circle (one size number) is what the step asks, but a dynamic square still counts for this card.

rubric.title: Make it bouncy
rubric.description: The ball's bounciness is set to 0.5 or more (the lab suggests near 1). A value under 0.5 is not met yet. Help: 5.2.11 (Bounciness and Friction)

rubric.title: Set friction
rubric.description: A sprite's friction, normally the ball's, is set to any value (the steps try 0, then 5; a very low value keeps it rolling). Help: 5.2.11 (Bounciness and Friction)
